analysis:
Examined all supplied metadata, patches, source and tests. The new workflow pins actions, checks tag/version compatibility, imports a team-selected signing identity, notarizes, verifies and publishes assets (.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml:37-203). Builder changes enforce signing and notarization credentials for release mode, reject preview/release combinations, preserve hardened runtime and enable validated signing (desktop-app/electron-builder.ts:20-68). Tests cover configuration gates, not final artifact security; changelog and developer documentation describe distribution without claiming serving qualification.
Relevant contracts are T-013/T-034/T-054 and A-017: Developer ID signing/notarization must not substitute for provider build qualification. No supplied change alters coordinator authorization, endpoint custody, encryption, prompts, cache isolation (T-041), billing or fan authority. No independently supported security regression was identified.
Integration should examine the release packaging scripts and bundled installer: npm ci/dist run with the imported CLI signing identity and notarization credentials available (workflow:84-130), and final CLI download verification remains outside this source scope. Verify that DMG/ZIP contents match the app checked at lines 160-171; the visible workflow checks ZIP existence/hash but does not inspect its contents. Keychain cleanup depends on KEYCHAIN_PATH exported only after successful import/identity resolution (117, 205-208); failure-path residue depends on runner isolation, which is not supplied. These are unverified contracts, not evidence of exploitable deployment settings.
Also reconcile manual-dispatch semantics: lines 51-56 select publication solely by ref type, so dispatch on an unpublished tag can publish despite the documented dry-run promise. This alone establishes a behavior mismatch, not adversarial access or an authorization bypass. Remaining review is limited to this new signing/distribution path; unchanged runtime controls were not audited.
